construction_note: This dataset does NOT exist pre-downloaded. You must construct it from public NVD/CVE records and GitHub commits. Follow the four-step protocol below.
construction_steps: Step 1 — Collect: Use the NVD REST API (https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0) to query CVE entries for C projects. Filter for entries with GitHub references. Use PyGithub or the GitHub REST API to fetch the associated commits.

Step 2 — Expand: For each CVE commit, search for additional related commits in the same repo using edit-distance heuristics on diff hunks or commit message keywords (e.g., 'fix', 'patch', 'CVE', 'security').

Step 3 — Filter & Pair: Keep only function-level changes (parse with tree-sitter or ctags). For each CVE, identify the earliest pre-patch function and the latest post-patch function in the patched branch. These form the (original_before, original_after) pair. Pair with a target-branch vulnerable function (unfixed variant) if multiple branches exist.
Step 4 — Split: Sort by commit date. Before 2023-08-23 → fine-tuning set. After 2023-08-23 → evaluation set.

recommended_scale.note: Full paper scale (2,842 fine-tuning / 694 evaluation CVEs) is not feasible in a single run. Use a reduced scope.
recommended_scale.minimal: 50 CVEs from popular C projects (Linux, OpenSSL, curl) — evaluation only with zero-shot LLM baselines
recommended_scale.medium: 200 CVEs — evaluation only with zero-shot LLM baselines
recommended_scale.full_with_gpu: 694 CVEs evaluation + 2,842 fine-tuning (requires GPU >=48GB for LoRA fine-tuning)

nvd_api.note: API key not required but rate-limited; add Nvd-Api-Key header if available

directory_layout.dataset_candidate/cve_patches/raw/: Raw CVE records and commit diffs

sample_record_format.target_branch_fix: <Human-written fix for target branch — evaluation only>
